jobs.prompt: Use the new worker token module tools/worker-token.mjs in the orchestrator-mode guard so that 'verified worker' can no longer be faked. In tools/shell-writes.mjs change isVerifiedSwarmWorkerCwd (and orchestratorWorkerSessionExempt, and every caller in tools/handbuild.mjs and tools/orchestrator-allow.mjs) so a session is a verified worker ONLY when the environment variable SWARM_WORKER_TOKEN holds a token that verifyWorkerToken accepts for the session's cwd (hash match, not revoked, not expired, cwd inside the recorded workspace). The environment variable SWARM_WORKER_RUN_ID alone, a cwd inside the swarm workspaces folder alone, or a run record alone must give NO exemption. verifyWorkerToken is async: if the guard path is synchronous, add a synchronous variant verifyWorkerTokenSync in tools/worker-token.mjs with the same checks (fs sync calls) and use it. A verified worker may write only inside ITS OWN workspace (the recorded workspace path): writes to another job's workspace, the repo root checkout, the swarm runs folder and the swarm ledger paths stay denied for a worker too; a worker's write outside its own workspace gets the existing deny text. The deny text for the orchestrator must not mention the token value. Update the six test files that set the run id environment variable themselves (tests/orchestrator-mode.test.mjs, tests/orchestrator-mode-review2.test.mjs, tests/orchestrator-mode-review3.test.mjs, tests/orchestrator-mode-review4.test.mjs, tests/orchestrator-mode-default.test.mjs, tests/orchestrator-allow.test.mjs) so any worker case uses a REAL token issued with issueWorkerToken for a real temp workspace and passes it in the environment, never only the run id; keep the same intent of each test. Add tests: run id env alone is not exempt; a cwd inside the workspaces folder alone is not exempt; a run record created by the orchestrator through swarm run plus the run id env plus cd into that workspace is not exempt (simulate by creating run folder, state file and workspace folder by hand, then check the guard denies a write); token for job A cannot write in job B's workspace or the repo root; revoked and expired tokens give no exemption. IMPORTANT: the repository's secret scanner blocks credential-looking literals in files: in tests build any fake token or secret value at run time (join or repeat) and never assign one to a name like token, secret or key as a literal. Do not use wildcard patterns or file-looking words in comments that name files that do not exist. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS from Opus review 7: (1) a verified worker may write ONLY under the real path of its own recorded workspace (run and job); this must hold with the hand-build guard on AND off (today with the hand-build guard off a verified worker may write anywhere, because the allow-list is skipped for verified workers: fix that path so the worker scope is enforced in every state); the worker's writes to the repo root checkout, to another job's workspace, to another run's workspace, and to any swarm runs, orchestrator-mode and handbuild folders are denied, and writes to the dot swarm orchestrator-mode and handbuild folders are denied for EVERY session including workers; shell writes with a relative path or a cd out of the workspace or git -C pointing out of the workspace are denied for workers too. (2) a session whose cwd is inside a workspace but without a valid token must NOT be exempt (the working-folder-only exemption in tools/orchestrator-allow.mjs around the allow-list skip is removed).
